member.summary: Compares two delegates for equality.
member.remarks:
This equality comparison differs from the default implementation of and in that it does not compare the delegate type. Different delegate types that reference the same target and have method signature and invocation list are considered equal.
For example:
Action<object, EventArgs> action = SomeMethod; EventHandler<EventArgs> eventHandler = SomeMethod;
// Using the default comparison bool isEqual = action.Equals(eventHandler); // FALSE
// Using DelegateEqualityComparer comparison var delegateSignatureEqualityComparer = new DelegateSignatureEqualityComparer(); isEqual = delegateSignatureEqualityComparer.Equals(action, eventHandler); // TRUE
private void SomeMethod(object, EventArgs) { }
The two delegates do not have to be of the same type in order to be considered equal.
Two are compared for equality as follows:
The values are compared using to ensure one of the following conditions is true:
If the two methods being compared are both static and are the same method on the same class, the methods are considered equal and the targets are also considered equal.
If the two methods being compared are instance methods and are the same method on the same object, the methods are considered equal.
Otherwise, the methods are not considered to be equal and the targets are also not considered to be equal.
The values are compared using to ensure one of the following conditions is true:
If the two delegate targets being compared are both (in case of static methods), the targets are considered equal and the targets are also considered equal.
If the two delegate targets being compared are the same instance, the targets are considered equal.
Otherwise, the delegate targets are not considered to be equal.
The invocation lists are compared to ensure all of the following conditions are satisfied:
Both invocation lists contain the same number of elements.
Both invocation lists are ordered exactly the same, where both rules 1) and 2) must be satisfied.
This means every element in the invocation list of the first delegate is equal to the corresponding element in the invocation list of the second delegate.
